description: The pink palace on the Buriganga was the residence of the Nawab family of Dhaka and is now a museum of period furniture, portraits and photographs. The riverside position explains why old Dhaka grew here: this was the commercial face of the city in the 19th century.
feeNote: Ticketed site — confirm the current entry fee and opening hours at the gate.

description: An unfinished Mughal fort begun in the 17th century, containing the tomb of Pari Bibi, a mosque and a bathhouse. The grounds are calm by Dhaka standards and best visited early morning.
feeNote: Ticketed site — confirm the current entry fee at the gate.

description: An 18th-century mosque in Armanitola decorated with blue star motifs in imported china clay, later extended in the 20th century. It is an active place of worship: dress modestly, remove shoes and avoid visiting during prayers.
feeNote: Free to enter; donations welcome. Active place of worship.

description: Built in the mid-15th century under Khan Jahan Ali, the Shat Gombuj Masjid is the centrepiece of the UNESCO-listed mosque city. Despite the name it carries 77 domes, and the tapering brick walls and terracotta mihrabs are the finest Sultanate work in Bengal.
feeNote: Free entry; modest dress required. Friday midday prayers restrict visitor access.

description: The largest Buddhist monastery south of the Himalayas, built under the Pala dynasty and abandoned around the 12th century. Its cross-shaped central shrine rises above 177 monastic cells arranged around a courtyard.
feeNote: Ticketed site with a museum — confirm current hours and fees on arrival.

description: A small national park south of Cox's Bazar where hills meet the sea. There is a waterfall in the monsoon, a short hill trail to a viewpoint, and good birdwatching in the early morning.
feeNote: Small entry ticket; confirm current fee at the gate. Waterfall flows mainly in monsoon.

description: A quieter stretch of coast about 30 km south of Cox's Bazar, known for coral stone and clear water at low tide. Far fewer people than the main beach; go with a driver you trust and return before dark.
feeNote: Public beach, no entry fee. Swimming not recommended beyond the shallows.

description: A ridge above the Sangu valley with wide views into the hills. The road up passes Chimbuk and tea gardens; mornings are clearest and clouds often sit below the viewpoint.
feeNote: Viewpoint/restaurant entry may be charged by the operator — confirm on arrival.

description: A hill lake near Ruma surrounded by forest and villages, reached by a rough road and a walk. Local legend gives the lake its name; the practical facts are steep trails, limited food and patchy phone signal.
feeNote: Local guide and community fees apply. Access depends on current area permissions.

description: A reservoir created by damming the Karnaphuli in the 1960s, now a landscape of forested islands and floating markets. Full-day boat trips from Rangamati town reach Rajban Bihar, Shuvolong and island bazaars.
feeNote: Boat fares are negotiated per trip — agree route, duration and total price first.

description: A 1,250-hectare rainforest park near Srimangal with walking trails, Hoolock gibbons and a long list of bird species. A licensed guide is required for the main trail and is worth the fee.
feeNote: Entry ticket and guide fee apply; confirm current rates at the gate.

description: Bangladesh's best-known freshwater swamp forest, about 26 km from Sylhet city. In the monsoon the trees stand in water and boats pass between them; in the dry season the roots are exposed and the experience is very different.
feeNote: Boat and entry fees apply; confirm the current rate and water level before going.

description: A 100 km² Ramsar wetland in Sunamganj, best explored by houseboat between November and February. Villagers move between seasonal islands; birdlife peaks in midwinter.
feeNote: Haor boats are chartered per trip — check safety equipment, life jackets and the total price.

description: The shrine of the 14th-century Sufi saint who is closely associated with the spread of Islam in Sylhet. The complex includes a mosque and is busy on Thursday evenings and during Urs.
feeNote: Free entry. Dress modestly; photography may be restricted inside.

description: The tomb of the 15th-century Sufi saint and city-builder, beside the large Ghora Dighi tank. The annual Urs draws pilgrims from across the region.
feeNote: Free entry. Modest dress required; busy during Urs.

description: A wide beach facing south, so both sunrise and sunset are visible from the sand. The surrounding villages are home to Rakhine and Hindu fishing families with distinct food and architecture.
feeNote: Public beach, no entry fee. Swimming is not recommended beyond the shallows.

description: The reef flat off Bangladesh's only coral island, best seen at low tide with a local guide. Coral is fragile and collecting it is illegal; several operators run responsible snorkelling trips.
feeNote: No reef fee; guide and boat costs apply. Do not touch or remove coral.
